project.name: HDF5
project.commit_note: Stage 01 reproduced against the staged ARVO workspace checkout `966454aac1231da7209ef81c11055d3312181f99` inside the running workspace container rather than metadata vulnerable commit `a0340338e53d4b34127a7e5356b28b1640f9414c`. That staged tree still contains the unfixed `H5O__cache_chk_deserialize()` / `H5O__chunk_deserialize()` / `H5O__cache_chk_serialize()` logic later hardened by `07e94155a7d456d663fe19a38851556117b5e315`, so all line anchors below use this staged vulnerable checkout.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42523860 (hdf5): Heap-buffer-overflow READ {*} found by fuzz target h5_extended_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42523860
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source in the ARVO workspace / staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 1808-byte witness with SHA-256 `e0ad984792ca23cf5ca56e4617615b8d0e786e320d64916ab00fe11e292b8cca` is an HDF5 file whose version-2 superblock decodes `ext_addr == 0x30`, `stored_eof == 0x710`, and `root_addr == 0x68`. HDF5 opens the superblock extension at `0x30` and, in `H5O__prefix_deserialize()`, decodes that object header as version 1 with `chunk0_size == 0x544`; `H5O__cache_get_final_load_size()` then requests `0x544 + 0x10 = 0x554` bytes, and `H5O__chunk_deserialize()` copies those bytes into `oh->chunk[0].image`. The vulnerable version-1 walker in `H5O__chunk_deserialize()` reads each 8-byte message header before any field-wise bounds check. After the real driver-info message at file offset `0x40`, it accepts a zero-sized pseudo-message at `0x68`, so the walk keeps reinterpreting raw chunk bytes as additional headers. Along that unchecked walk the same staged bytes yield pseudo-headers with `id == H5O_CONT_ID` at offsets `0xa8`, `0xd8`, `0x138`, `0x168`, `0x1e0`, `0x228`, `0x258`, `0x388`, `0x3f8`, `0x448`, and `0x530`; the bodies behind all but `0x448` decode `cont->size == 0`. The pseudo-header at `0x448` decodes a continuation body with `addr == 0x200` and `size == 0x400`, and source semantics carry that descriptor into `cont_msg_info`, `chk_udata.size`, the H5AC_OHDR_CHK initial load size, and the chunk-proxy cache-entry length `len == 1024` that later reaches `H5O__cache_chk_serialize()`. Separately, the saved ASan allocation stack proves that the crashing source pointer came from an 8-byte user region allocated at `src/H5Ocache.c:1321` on the same continuation-chunk load path. The staged static artifacts do not identify the exact pseudo-descriptor or later source-level reindex/rebind step that makes the 1024-byte serialize read at `src/H5Ocache.c:875` use that 8-byte region, so the parser-to-1024-byte length chain is closed but the final source-buffer alias remains unresolved in Stage 02. The patch repairs the parser side by threading explicit input lengths into `H5O__prefix_deserialize()` / `H5O__chunk_deserialize()` and adding `H5_IS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW(...)` checks before each prefix and message-header field read.

source.description: First project-side consumption of the superblock-extension object-header bytes that selects the vulnerable version-1 parse layout.
source.value_from: Exactly the staged 1808-byte HDF5 `poc` with SHA-256 `e0ad984792ca23cf5ca56e4617615b8d0e786e320d64916ab00fe11e292b8cca`. The v2 superblock decodes `ext_addr == 0x30`, and the first byte at that object-header address is `0x01`, so this statement selects `H5O_VERSION_1`.
source.note: The libFuzzer entry is only the harness boundary. Vulnerability-relevant parser state begins when HDF5 decodes the superblock extension's object-header prefix from attacker-controlled file bytes.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The version-1 object-header walker reads `id`, `mesg_size`, `flags`, and the reserved bytes from `chunk_image` before verifying that those header fields themselves fit inside the chunk, so raw chunk bytes can be promoted into pseudo-message and continuation state.
root_cause.note: At file offset `0x68`, this logic decodes `id = 0x002d`, `mesg_size = 0`, and `flags = 0` from bytes that are not a real message header. The patch adds `H5_IS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW(...)` guards before each prefix field read.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The chunk-proxy serializer copies `len` bytes from `chk_proxy->oh->chunk[chk_proxy->chunkno].image`; the saved crash proves `len == 1024` while the faulting source pointer is immediately past an 8-byte user region allocated earlier at `H5O__chunk_deserialize:1321`.
sink.note: Stage 02 closes the source path from the positive-size pseudo-continuation at `0x448` to `len == 1024`, but not the later descriptor or proxy rebind that made this serialize read source from the 8-byte user region named by ASan.

tainted_value_origin.description: After the prefix-decoded `chunk0_size` determines the first-chunk extent, this copy turns the attacker-controlled superblock-extension bytes into heap-backed `oh->chunk[0].image` state that the vulnerable v1 walker later interprets as message headers and continuation bodies.

parser_admitted.description: After superblock decode sets `ext_addr == 0x30`, the saved run reaches superblock-extension object-header lookup here and enters the H5O cache parser path.

asan_allocation_observed.description: The saved ASan allocation stack identifies this line as the allocator for the faulting source pointer's 8-byte user region on the same `H5O_msg_exists -> H5O_protect -> H5O__cache_chk_deserialize -> H5O__chunk_deserialize` continuation-load path. The staged static artifacts do not localize which pseudo-descriptor or later rebind produced that call.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness writes the exact witness to disk and opens it read-write; superblock decode routes file open to the superblock-extension object header at `0x30`.
HDF5 decodes the extension object header as version 1 with `chunk0_size == 0x544`, sizes the first object-header read from those values, and materializes chunk 0 into `oh->chunk[0].image`.

The vulnerable v1 header walk accepts a zero-sized pseudo-message, keeps scanning raw chunk bytes, and eventually records a pseudo-continuation at `0x448` whose body decodes to `addr == 0x200` and `size == 0x400`; source semantics carry that descriptor into a 1024-byte chunk-load/cache length.
Because the file is opened with write intent, `H5F_open` flushes tagged superblock-extension metadata before returning to the harness.

The flush-time chunk-proxy serializer is reached with `len == 1024`, but the saved runtime evidence separately proves that the faulting source pointer belongs to an 8-byte `H5O__chunk_deserialize` user region on the same continuation-load path; the exact source-level alias/reindex step remains unresolved in the staged artifacts.

fine_trace.note: Harness step. The exact staged witness is written verbatim to a temporary file and opened read-write. That write intent is the control fact that later makes `H5F_open` flush tagged superblock-extension metadata before returning.

From the v2 superblock bytes, HDF5 decodes `base_addr = 0`, `ext_addr = 0x30`, `stored_eof = 0x710`, and `root_addr = 0x68`. `ext_addr` is the attacker-controlled object-header address later opened as the superblock extension.
Because `sblock->ext_addr` is defined, `H5F__super_read()` opens the superblock extension at `0x30` and asks whether its object header contains `H5O_DRVINFO_ID`, entering the H5O cache parser path.

Source step. The first byte of the superblock-extension object header is `0x01`, so HDF5 decodes this header as `H5O_VERSION_1`. That version choice selects the vulnerable v1 prefix and 8-byte message-header layout used later in the walk.
The same v1 prefix bytes decode `udata->chunk0_size = 0x544` from file offset `0x38`, establishing how many attacker-controlled bytes HDF5 will treat as chunk 0.
Using the prefix-decoded v1 header size (`0x10`) and `chunk0_size = 0x544`, `H5O__cache_get_final_load_size()` requests `0x554` bytes for the full prefix+chunk-0 image.
The first-chunk loader carries that same prefix-decoded size into in-memory object-header state and sets `oh->chunk[0].size = 0x554`.

HDF5 copies the 16-byte v1 prefix plus `0x544` bytes of chunk-0 data into `oh->chunk[0].image`; after the 16-byte prefix skip, the vulnerable walk starts at file offset `0x40` inside this heap-backed buffer.

Root-cause step. On the v1 path, the walker reads `id`, `mesg_size`, `flags`, and the three reserved bytes from `chunk_image` before any bounds check on those header fields. After the real driver-info message at file offset `0x40`, the next 8-byte slot at `0x68` is reinterpreted as `id = 0x002d`, `mesg_size = 0`, `flags = 0`.

Because that pseudo-header advertises `mesg_size == 0`, the only pre-fix extent check does not reject it. The walker advances only by the 8-byte header and keeps treating later raw chunk bytes as more message headers.

Later in the same unchecked v1 walk, several 8-byte slots decode `id == H5O_CONT_ID`; the staged bytes reach such pseudo-headers at file offsets `0xa8`, `0xd8`, `0x138`, `0x168`, `0x1e0`, `0x228`, `0x258`, `0x388`, `0x3f8`, `0x448`, and `0x530`. The earlier ones later decode `cont->size == 0`; the slot at `0x448` is the later positive-size continuation path traced below.

For the pseudo-continuation rooted at file offset `0x448`, the 32-byte body at `0x450` decodes to `cont->addr = 0x200` and `cont->size = 0x400`. This is the only positive-size continuation body closed by the staged walk; the other continuation-like headers above decode `cont->size == 0`.
When that continuation body is accepted, HDF5 predicts the future chunk index for the chunk it points to by setting `cont->chunkno` to the next continuation-chunk slot.
The loader records the decoded continuation descriptor in `cont_msg_info`, preserving `addr = 0x200`, `size = 0x400`, and the predicted `chunkno` for later chunk loads.
During continuation processing, HDF5 copies that descriptor into `chk_udata` and asks the metadata cache to load an `H5AC_OHDR_CHK` entry from `addr = 0x200` with `size = 0x400`.
The H5AC_OHDR_CHK loader uses the continuation descriptor's size verbatim as its requested on-disk image length, so this local path asks the cache to read `0x400` bytes.

On the statically closed `0x448` path, this continuation load would append a new chunk whose `chunk_size` is `0x400` and bind the returned proxy to that new `oh->chunk[...]` slot. That local source path therefore stays 1024 bytes wide, which does not by itself explain the separate 8-byte user region named by ASan.
The metadata cache persists the same `len == 0x400` on the loaded chunk-proxy entry, which is the value later passed to the serialize callback as `len`.
Because the harness opened the file with write intent, `H5F_open()` dirties the superblock and immediately flushes tagged metadata for the superblock extension before returning.
The metadata cache enters the flush-time chunk-proxy serializer and passes the cached entry length as the `len` argument. For the closed `0x448` descriptor path, that `len` is 1024.

Sink. AddressSanitizer reports `READ of size 1024` here and says the faulting source pointer lies immediately after an 8-byte user region allocated earlier at `H5O__chunk_deserialize:1321` on the same continuation-chunk load path. The staged static artifacts do not isolate the exact pseudo-descriptor or later chunk-proxy reindex/rebind that makes this 1024-byte serialize read source from that 8-byte region.

allocation_context.note: The saved ASan report says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of an 8-byte region allocated here.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Partially. The root cause explains how malformed version-1 object-header bytes fabricate continuation descriptors on the same `H5O_msg_exists -> H5O_protect -> H5O__cache_chk_deserialize -> H5O__chunk_deserialize` load path named by ASan. The saved allocation context itself is a later 8-byte user-region allocation at `H5O__chunk_deserialize:1321`, but the staged static artifacts do not localize which descriptor or reindex/rebind made the serializer use that specific buffer.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes for both observed halves of the run. The saved crash stack is the flush-time half (`H5O__cache_chk_serialize -> H5C__generate_image -> H5F_flush_tagged_metadata -> H5F_open`), and the saved allocation stack is a continuation-chunk load half (`H5O__chunk_deserialize -> H5O__cache_chk_deserialize -> H5O_protect -> H5O_msg_exists -> H5F__super_read`). The rebuilt trace closes the prefix-decode and `0x448`-descriptor-to-`len == 1024` chain while explicitly leaving the final 8-byte source-buffer alias unresolved.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Partially. The staged bytes are closed through `oh->version == 1`, `chunk0_size == 0x544`, the unchecked zero-sized pseudo-message, the positive-size continuation body at `0x448`, and the resulting `len == 1024` that reaches the sink. ASan separately proves the source pointer at the sink comes from an 8-byte user region allocated at `H5O__chunk_deserialize:1321` on the same load path, but the exact descriptor or later `chk_proxy->chunkno` rebind that joins those facts is not recoverable from Stage 02 artifacts.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42523860 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` file to `/out/h5_extended_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1024` with stack `H5O__cache_chk_serialize -> H5C__generate_image -> H5C__flush_single_entry`.

format.name: malformed HDF5 file
format.contract: Exactly the staged 1808-byte binary with SHA-256 `e0ad984792ca23cf5ca56e4617615b8d0e786e320d64916ab00fe11e292b8cca`. The verified trigger semantics are limited to this exact file: its version-2 superblock decodes `ext_addr == 0x30`, the extension object header at `0x30` decodes as version 1 with `chunk0_size == 0x544`, the vulnerable v1 walk accepts the zero-sized pseudo-header at `0x68`, and later continuation-like pseudo-headers include the positive-size body at `0x448 -> addr 0x200, size 0x400`. Stage 01 separately proves that the same run reaches an 8-byte `H5O__chunk_deserialize` allocation before the final 1024-byte serialize overread, but Stage 02 cannot recover the exact source-level descriptor or rebind that joins that 8-byte region to the sink. This contract therefore stays at the exact witness and observed parser/flush path and does not generalize to neighboring HDF5 layouts or field values.
